jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Customer Milestones Delivery
jobs.description:
Who we are

Pronto AI is a global leader in commercializing autonomous vehicle (AV) technology, deploying Autonomous Haulage Systems (AHS) that automate operations in mines, quarries, and construction sites worldwide. While much of the industry remains in R&D, we deliver real, production-ready autonomy that is already operating in the field.

We are on a mission to make mining operations safer, smarter, and more efficient through cutting-edge technology, and we are building toward becoming the world’s first profitable AV technology company.

About the role

The Customer Milestones Delivery TPM owns a single tracked calendar of every customer-facing commitment across Pronto's active deployments, and is the one consistent voice when a date is at risk or has to move. Today, customer dates live across scattered trackers and get communicated by whichever team happens to be closest to the customer at the time. This role replaces that with one owner, one calendar, and one voice.

What you’ll do

Milestone Tracking

- Build and maintain a single tracked calendar of every customer-facing date across all active sites — kickoff, go-live, ramp milestones, contractual deadlines — replacing the scattered trackers in use today.

- Keep the calendar current by pulling status directly from the teams executing against each date, not by waiting for it to be reported.

Early-Warning & Risk Flagging

- Flag a date at risk before it slips, based on leading indicators from execution teams, not after the customer has already noticed.

- Build the judgment to tell a normal schedule variance from a real risk, so early warnings carry weight instead of becoming noise.

Customer Communication

- Be the one consistent voice on customer timeline changes, so a customer hears about a slipped or moved date the same way, from the same source, every time.

- Own the hard conversation when a date has to move: what changed, why, and the new commitment — rather than leaving it to whichever team is in the room.

- Coordinate with Sales, Deployment, and Customer Success so the message a customer hears matches what internal teams actually believe will happen.

What we’re looking for

- External or customer-facing program management experience — has personally owned a hard conversation about a slipped date with a paying customer.

- Rigor to build and maintain a live tracking system across several concurrent sites without letting it go stale.

- Proactive by default: flags risk before being asked, rather than only status-reporting after the fact.

- Strong written and verbal communication, comfortable being the consistent point of contact on sensitive timeline conversations.

Nice to have

- Experience in a deployment, customer success, or delivery role for a hardware or field-deployed technology product.

- Experience with autonomous vehicle, robotics, or heavy industrial equipment customer programs.

- Familiarity with Linear or a similar tool for pulling execution status directly from delivery teams.

Why join us

- Work on real, production-deployed autonomy.

- Build technology that directly improves safety, efficiency, and productivity.

- Tackle complex challenges in demanding, real-world environments.

- Be part of a fast-moving team with high ownership and impact.

- See your work deployed and making a difference in the field.

- Collaborate closely with experienced engineers and industry operators.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our San Francisco office location. As a company driven by innovation and continuous change, close collaboration is essential. We’re constantly reimagining our industry, creating new products, and refining our processes, and we do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

The base salary range for this role is $122,000 - $151,000 per year.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for equity awards.

Benefits Summary (USA Full-Time Exempt Employees):

- Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, and Life Insurance

- Flexible Spending Account / Health Savings Account Options

- 401(k)

- Equity

- Sick Time, Unlimited Flexible Time Off, and Paid Holidays

- Paid Parental Leave

- Pre-Tax Commuter Benefit Plan

- Team lunch in our SoMa office every Tuesday and Thursday

Benefits are subject to change at the company's discretion.
Pronto accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Hardware & Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Who we are

Pronto AI is a global leader in commercializing autonomous vehicle (AV) technology, deploying Autonomous Haulage Systems (AHS) that automate operations in mines, quarries, and construction sites worldwide. While much of the industry remains in R&D, we deliver real, production-ready autonomy that is already operating in the field.

We are on a mission to make mining operations safer, smarter, and more efficient through cutting-edge technology, and we are building toward becoming the world’s first profitable AV technology company.

About the role

The Hardware & Manufacturing TPM owns the queue where onsite hardware and QC issues meet engineering — the seam between the build floor (OEM production lines, upfit partners, kitting) and the teams that own the design. This role triages incoming hardware issues across active builds, on-road transport truck kitting and off-road mining kit installs alike, decides what escalates and to whom, and owns inventory issues before they hold up a build.

Today those reports land in a shared channel with no consistent triage, so a cosmetic issue and a line-stopping one compete for attention in whatever order they arrive. This role replaces that with a single owned queue.

What you’ll do

Intake & Triage

- Own a single intake queue for hardware and QC issues reported from build lines and field sites, replacing today's mix of ad hoc Slack messages and DMs.

- Triage every incoming issue by severity and impact — distinguishing a line-stopping defect from a cosmetic one — rather than working items in the order they arrive.

- Set and hold response-time expectations for build partners and plant contacts.

Dev-Queue Prioritization

- Prioritize the engineering dev queue against what's actually blocking a build or a site, not against whichever issue was reported most recently.

- Identify when several individual tickets are the same underlying defect, and roll them into one engineering fix rather than let them get worked separately.

Onsite QC & Inventory Escalation

- Own escalation for onsite QC failures and inventory shortages — the shared point between the field/build floor and engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing.

- Track recurring hardware defects (wrong part revisions, bracket or jig issues, harness defects) back to their root cause, and escalate to the owning team: engineering, supplier, or the line itself.

- Escalate hardware issues affecting truck builds across both on-road transport upfit lines and off-road mining kit installs.

What we’re looking for

- Hands-on hardware, manufacturing, or field-ops background — has worked the floor, not just reviewed reports about it.

- Comfortable as the triage point between site or build partners and engineering: thick skin, high urgency, able to make a prioritization call with incomplete information.

- Has stood up an intake or QC process from scratch, not just operated one someone else built.

- Track record working with vehicle or heavy-equipment hardware (wiring harnesses, sensor/compute mounting, electromechanical assemblies).

Nice to have

- Experience with on-road commercial vehicle (Class 8 truck) upfit, kitting, or OEM production-line environments.

- Experience with off-road or heavy industrial equipment (mining, construction) hardware builds.

- Familiarity with supplier and inventory escalation, and part-revision control.

- Experience with Linear or a similar ticketing tool for tracking build issues to closure.

Why join us

- Build technology that directly improves safety, efficiency, and productivity.

- Tackle complex challenges in demanding, real-world environments.

- Be part of a fast-moving team with high ownership and impact.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - New Product Integration
jobs.description:
Who we are

Pronto AI is a global leader in commercializing autonomous vehicle (AV) technology, deploying Autonomous Haulage Systems (AHS) that automate operations in mines, quarries, and construction sites worldwide. While much of the industry remains in R&D, we deliver real, production-ready autonomy that is already operating in the field.

We are on a mission to make mining operations safer, smarter, and more efficient through cutting-edge technology, and we are building toward becoming the world’s first profitable AV technology company.

About the role

The NPI TPM owns the handoff between engineering and the field: taking a released kit design through first builds, pilot units, and full production ramp, across Hardware, EE, Firmware, Robotics, Software, Operations, and Manufacturing. This role sequences every new kit program end to end, whether it's a new sensor mast for an off-road mining platform or a new upfit kit for an on-road Class 8 tractor, and owns launch readiness for each one.

This is a cross-functional execution role, not a design role. The NPI TPM does not do the engineering; they make sure every team's work lands in the right order, dependencies are tracked before they cause a slip, and each program clears its build and QC gates before it moves forward.

What you’ll do
Program Sequencing & Cross-Team Coordination :

-

- Sequence each new kit program end to end across Hardware, EE, Firmware, Robotics, Software, Operations, and Manufacturing, so no team starts a step before its inputs are ready.

- Own the master schedule for each active kit program, keeping design, build, and manufacturing milestones synchronized across teams.

- Run program syncs and design reviews, and drive open decisions to closure rather than let them linger across teams

Cross-Program Dependency Tracking

-

- Track dependencies and shared resources across concurrent kit programs, and flag conflicts (like one team supporting two programs at once) before they cause a slip.

- Maintain a single source of truth for program status, blockers, and interdependencies.

- Escalate resourcing or sequencing conflicts to engineering and program leadership with a clear recommendation, not just a flag.

Launch Readiness & Build Transitions

- Own the readiness criteria for each program gate: first-article build, pilot build, cut-in and ECO execution, and full production ramp.

- Partner with NPI and Manufacturing Engineering on DFM/DFA feedback, work instructions, and build/QC checklists, so designs released by engineering are actually buildable at volume.

- Drive the go/no-go decision at each gate, and own the retrospective when a gate is missed.

Field & Manufacturing Feedback Loop

- Serve as the link between build and field issues and the engineering teams that own the design, closing the loop on defects found during test and pilot builds.

- Make sure lessons from one kit program's build issues carry into the next program's design and process, instead of being rediscovered from scratch.

What we’re looking for

- 5+ years in technical program or product management for hardware, with direct experience taking a hardware or electromechanical product from design release through pilot build and into production.

- Broad technical fluency across hardware, EE, firmware/software, and manufacturing, enough to sequence work and understand real blockers, without needing to be the deepest expert on any one team.

- Track record owning a program schedule across four or more cross-functional teams with competing priorities.

- Comfortable in ambiguity, including building a sequencing and tracking process where one doesn't fully exist yet.

- Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to run a design review or gate meeting and drive it to a decision.

Nice to have

- Experience with autonomous vehicle, robotics, or heavy industrial equipment kit programs, on-road transport or off-road/mining.

- Experience with PLM or configuration management systems, BOM control, and ECO processes.

- Familiarity with Linear or a similar tool for cross-team ticket and dependency tracking.

- Prior experience at a company scaling from a handful to a double-digit number of concurrent hardware programs.

Why join us

- Work on real, production-deployed autonomy.

- Build technology that directly improves safety, efficiency, and productivity.

- Tackle complex challenges in demanding, real-world environments.

- Be part of a fast-moving team with high ownership and impact.

- See your work deployed and making a difference in the field.

- Collaborate closely with experienced engineers and industry operators.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our San Francisco office location. As a company driven by innovation and continuous change, close collaboration is essential. We’re constantly reimagining our industry, creating new products, and refining our processes, and we do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.
